title: Profile-Stable Buffered Multiplicity Factoring in Four Dimensions
summary: Multiplicity factoring is usually formulated for child families at comparable scales. For children of mixed geometry, thickening at the shortest parent scale produces nonuniform inflation ratios, and a single worst-case replacement does not preserve the natural density normalization. We prove a multiplicity-factoring theorem for finite indexed convex parent--child families in $\mathbb{R}^4$ that accommodates arbitrary child shapes, scales, orientations, aspect ratios, and repetitions.
